transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Time: 09:30 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jared Liu (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (Redwood Solutions Eng); Olivia Chen (Acme PM), Rajiv Singh (Acme Backend), Tara O'Neal (Acme Sec), Ben Park (Acme Data), Eric Yu (Acme Frontend)

Summary: quick sync on SDK integration for tool/function calls and structured output. Reviewed results from last week's tests, discussed hangups around JSON schema validation and a few unexpected tokens in streaming responses, and aligned on next steps for benchmarks and security artifacts.

Topics: SDK function-calling, structured output schemas, streaming/parsing on frontend, latency & batching, hosted vs dedicated, security/KMS/audit logs, next steps for pilot scale tests.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jared Liu: Hey everyone thanks for making time, we'll do a quick 45 minute sync. Maya and Carlos from my side. Oliva?
[00:08] Olivia Chen: Yep, thanks Jared. Quick recap we ran the SDK integration branch Rajiv pushed last week, got some mixed results — structured outputs are mostly good but we saw occasional malformed JSON when responses stream.
[00:20] Maya Patel: Ok, that's consistent with what we saw on our end in the dev harness. Streaming plus partial function outputs can cause a stray comma or truncated object if the client doesn't buffer until final token. Are you using the SDK's structuredOutput helper or parsing manually?
[00:34] Rajiv Singh: We're parsing manually right now; we started with a quick parser on the frontend to handle partial chunks. We tried Redwood's structured mode but had trouble mapping nested arrays to our internal schema.
[00:47] Carlos Mendez: Got it. Two common patterns: 1) use Redwood SDK structured output with a JSON schema so the runtime will attempt to conform the output, 2) keep streaming enabled but buffer until the SDK emits a final 'output_complete' event. The SDK snippets we shared last week show both approaches.
[01:05] Ben Park: The malformed JSON appears in maybe 2-3% of responses in our 10k sample, usually when there's an inline code block or a long enumerated list.
[01:14] Maya Patel: Sounds like tokenization boundaries — long lists increase chance of tokens being split mid-structure. Two quick mitigations: raise max_tokens buffer so model doesn't truncate mid-object, and use the SDK's validateStructured call after completion which will try to repair common issues. We'll include an example.
[01:29] Tara O'Neal: From security side, one ask: if we move to private deployment will the structured outputs ever touch Redwood logs? We need guarantees for PII handling for the pilot.
[01:40] Jared Liu: Short answer — hosted default logs minimal telemetry but you can opt out and enable private deployment where logs stay in your VPC, and we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key control. We'll share the SOC2 docs and the KMS integration notes.
[01:52] Tara O'Neal: Great, please share the artifacts.
[01:55] Olivia Chen: Back to function calling — we wired the SDK to call our internal product search API as a tool. Works for most cases, but sometimes the model suggests a slightly different tool signature and the SDK rejects the call. It returns a schema mismatch and we log an error.
[02:10] Maya Patel: That's expected if model outputs don't match the declared function schema. Two strategies: 1) tighten the function signature in the SDK (types + required fields) and return error to user for manual correction, or 2) use Redwood's function coercion option which will try to coerce values into the schema when safe. Coercion helps when the model returns strings for numbers, etc.
[02:28] Eric Yu: For the frontend we need a stable streaming format so we can progressively render cards. Is there a recommended event model in the SDK for tool call start / tool call result / structured chunk?
[02:40] Carlos Mendez: Yes — SDK emits events: tool_call_start, tool_call_result (with corresponding tool metadata), structured_chunk, and output_complete. We can add the sample dashboard event tracing to the example repo so you can wire UI updates to those events.
[02:54] Rajiv Singh: Another practical question: what's the latency impact when we enable structured validation vs raw streaming? We saw an average +60ms in our quick runs.
[03:02] Maya Patel: Structured validation is an async step — if you run it synchronously in the request path you'll add overhead proportional to validation complexity. For most workloads it's 30-150ms depending on payload size; for tiny payloads it's smaller. For 1k QPS scale we recommend using async post-processing for heavy validations or offload to a background worker to preserve tail latency.
[03:22] Olivia Chen: That ties into cost too — validation and retries increase token usage. We want to understand hosted costs vs dedicated commit.
[03:30] Jared Liu: Right — hosting is simplest for pilot; compute + validation costs are metered. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and you can push validation into the same private pool to reduce egress. We'll send a cost model example comparing a hosted metered run vs dedicated reserved capacity for your 1k qps pattern.
[03:47] Ben Park: Also want to ensure caching won't invalidate structured outputs — e.g., prefix caching or KV cache for repeated prompts.
[03:55] Maya Patel: Caching is safe if prompts and prompt context are identical. For structured outputs, we recommend deterministic seeds or template-driven prompts and then apply prefix/KV caching for pre-computed sections (e.g., product metadata). We can show a caching config that only caches the deterministic prefix.
[04:12] Rajiv Singh: We attempted a tiny canary on Redwood hosted and saw a spike in latency at 95th percentile when parallelism increased — maybe because of batching?
[04:21] Carlos Mendez: Batching can hurt tail latency when request mix has small fast requests and some long token responses. Use adaptive batching and set max batch latency to a low value for latency sensitive routes. We can propose per-route policies in the config.
[04:36] Olivia Chen: On the SDK bits can you walk through the code example you mentioned?
[04:40] Maya Patel: Sure. High level snippet: register function schemas in the SDK, declare tool endpoints with expected types, enable structuredOutput: {schema: your_json_schema, mode: 'strict'|'coerce'|'repair'}, and wire listeners for structured_chunk and output_complete. In the example repo we include Node + Python samples and a small React streaming renderer.
[04:58] Eric Yu: Will the SDK sample show how to handle partial structured chunks that arrive out of order? We saw some chunk reordering in our websockets under poor mobile network conditions.
[05:07] Carlos Mendez: The SDK gives chunk sequence ids and a final ordering step. If the transport reorders you should reorder client-side by chunk id before parsing. We'll highlight that in the sample.
[05:18] Olivia Chen: A small bug we hit — sometimes the SDK's validateStructured returns a repaired object but the repaired fields are not annotated so we can't show warnings in the UI. Is there a plan to surface diffs?
[05:30] Maya Patel: Yes, there's a validation metadata option in the SDK where the validateStructured API can return metadata: {repaired:true, repair_reason: 'missing_field', original_fragment: '...'} . Seems like you didn't enable metadata in your call. We'll show how to enable metadata in the examples.
[05:46] Rajiv Singh: From backend perspective, we got a 413-like error when trying to send a 200kb context blob for a single request — whoops. What are best practices for large context?
[05:57] Carlos Mendez: For large contexts: use external vector store for embeddings and only pass the top-K condensed context, or use Redwood's chunked context upload + reference handle pattern where you upload large docs once and pass a document handle. We'll include the docs link.
[06:14] Tara O'Neal: Security question again — audit logs: can you confirm what is captured for tool calls? We need end-to-end traceability.
[06:23] Jared Liu: Audit logs capture request metadata, tool_call events, and whether structured validation passed or failed. For Private deployments you can direct logs to your SIEM and configure retention. We'll share the audit schema and sample logs.
[06:36] Olivia Chen: Cool. Any major blockers on our side before next week?
[06:40] Rajiv Singh: Main blocker is sharing our sample prompts and schema; we'll do that by Friday. Also need the example repo to try the structured metadata flow.
[06:48] Maya Patel: We'll prioritize the sample repo and include a test harness that runs 10k samples and outputs malformed-rate, avg latency, and token usage. Use that to replicate your 2-3% malformed rate.
[07:01] Carlos Mendez: Also want to run a small throughput test — 1k qps with mixed payload sizes — and compare hosted vs dedicated latency and cost. Suggest 1 hour run in non-prod.
[07:12] Olivia Chen: That sounds right. Also re: legal/procurement — if we go dedicated we need SOW and pricing; Jared will follow up.
[07:19] Jared Liu: I'll send a preliminary price band and a dedicated configuration doc after this call.
[07:24] Ben Park: One more thing — embedding vs model call frequency: for reranking we may want to precompute embeddings and do a hybrid approach. Any notes?
[07:31] Maya Patel: Hybrid approach recommended: precompute embeddings for catalog items and only call model for composition/formatting. That's cheaper and lower latency. We'll add a section in the repo.
[07:41] Eric Yu: For UI error handling if structured repair happens, we'll show a yellow caution card. If schema coercion changes a numeric ID we want to flag it.
[07:52] Carlos Mendez: That's sensible — validation metadata will indicate repaired fields. We'll send examples.
[07:58] Olivia Chen: Ok let's recap quick.
[08:02] Jared Liu: Recap: Redwood to share example repo with SDK function calling and structured-output tests (Maya lead). Jared to send SOC2/KMS docs and preliminary pricing. Carlos to run latency/cost estimate and coordinate the 1 hour throughput test. Acme to share prompts and JSON schema by 2026-03-27. We'll reconvene after the throughput test.
[08:21] Olivia Chen: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[08:25] Tara O'Neal: Thanks.
[08:27] Jared Liu: Thanks everyone — meeting adjourned.
